findings.title: getClientsWithPermission never returns individual clients and can return the literal 'Clients'
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission enumerates resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...). Per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (line 104) via resourceStore.create(...) without setting a type, so they never match the type filter. Only the all-clients resource matches, because init() sets its type. Consequence: when the scope is granted on all clients, the method adds the resource name "Clients" to the result as if it were a client id, and no individual client id is ever returned. Set the type when per-client resources are created, or look them up another way.

findings.title: Negative per-client VIEW policy cannot hide a client from an admin with all-clients VIEW
findings.body: canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() (the all-clients VIEW check) succeeds, before evaluating the client's own resource. Every other per-client check goes through hasPermission(client, ...), which uses the per-client resource when it exists and so honours negative policies. The user resource tests (testViewUserPermission) expect a per-object negative policy to override an all-objects positive permission. Here, an admin with all-clients VIEW and a NEGATIVE VIEW policy on a specific client still sees and can GET that client, and it still appears in listings. The short-circuit should be removed or the per-client result should take precedence.

findings.title: Existing FGAP v2 realms never receive the new Clients resource type or scopes
findings.body: init() returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms created before this change therefore never get the 'Clients' resource type resource or the new scopes configure, map-roles-client-scope and map-roles-composite. No migration is in this diff. Consequences: creating a client permission fails with ModelException("No scopes found.") (line 108), and getScope() throws 'Scope [...] does not exist'. Also, in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, ...) (services ClientPermissionsV2.java line 219), a missing 'Clients' resource makes getResourceTypeResource return null, and that null is passed to getPolicyStore().findByResource, which will likely throw an NPE. The String-based hasPermission on line 244 null-checks the same lookup, so the two paths behave inconsistently. Add an upgrade step or null-check the resource.

findings.title: Client-removal cleanup is skipped in V2-only deployments, leaving stale per-client resources
findings.body: The whole listener body is now gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1). Deployments that enable only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (the mode management()/evaluator() select V2 for) therefore skip ClientRemovedEvent handling entirely. Per-client resources named by the deleted client's UUID, and scope permissions referencing them, persist after the client is deleted. The guard should check the feature that actually selects the implementation, or V2 should implement the cleanup.

findings.title: Deleting any client fails when both fine-grained feature flags are enabled
findings.body: The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2. Its setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2.java line 193). The listener is gated only on the V1 flag, but evaluator()/management() prefer V2 whenever the V2 flag is set, so the two flags can coexist. In that configuration every client deletion propagates the exception and fails. The V2 implementation should be a no-op here, or the event handler should skip V2.

findings.title: Many ClientPermissionEvaluator methods throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2 mode
findings.body: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, which throws UnsupportedOperationException from canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, the *Permission(...) factories, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions. Before this PR, V2 mode used the V1 ClientPermissions implementation for these calls, which returned values instead of throwing. Any caller that reaches these methods in V2 mode now gets an uncaught exception, which surfaces as a 500 rather than a denial. canExchangeTo is the most exposed: it is part of the evaluator contract and is used by client-to-client token-exchange logic. getEvaluationContext (line 262) is an unused private helper that looks intended for canExchangeTo, so the method seems to have been left unfinished.

findings.title: getResourceName has no CLIENTS branch, so client permissions get a null display name
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases only USERS. For CLIENTS it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). That value is never set for per-client resources, which are named by the client UUID (line 104), and it is also unset for the all-clients 'Clients' resource. The result is null for client permissions. The USERS branch returns 'All users' for the type resource and the username for a user resource. The CLIENTS equivalents (an 'All clients' label and the client's clientId) are missing.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireView() says it returns a boolean, but it is a void method that throws
findings.body: The Javadoc for requireView() reads 'Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.' The method is void and is meant to throw ForbiddenException when canView() returns false. The same mistake appears on requireViewClientScopes() (line 101). Implementers reading this doc, including the V2 class, could easily get the contract backwards.

findings.title: New client tests omit client-scope checks, getClientsWithPermission and per-client negative policies
findings.body: The added tests cover per-client and all-clients MANAGE, VIEW, CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. Nothing exercises canManage/canView(ClientScopeModel), MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, getClientsWithPermission, or a NEGATIVE per-client policy overriding an all-clients permission. The getClientsWithPermission type-filter bug and the canView short-circuit would both have been caught by tests of these paths.
